title: GTM Engineer
description: About Kernel Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this? Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier. Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust. Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent Kernel ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Notion already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them. We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 12x YoY . The Role We're looking for a GTM Engineer to build the systems that take Kernel to $100m+ ARR. You'll own the infrastructure behind how we find, sell to and grow customers, from Salesforce and outbound to forecasting, renewals and expansion. This is a hands-on builder role, not a traditional RevOps support function. You'll work like a product engineer for GTM: find the biggest constraint on growth, turn a messy commercial problem into a working system, ship it quickly and improve it using real results. You do not need to be a software engineer, but you do need to be able to build with Salesforce, Clay, APIs, automation platforms and AI tools rather than waiting for someone else to do it. You'll also be Kernel's own internal customer , using Kernel to build an AI-native revenue engine, pressure-test the product in real workflows and turn what you learn into useful feedback for Product and Engineering. You'll report to Arvin Ashrafi, Head of Finance & Operations , and work closely with Sales leadership and the wider GTM team. What You'll Be Doing Build a better outbound engine: improve account targeting, signals, enrichment, prioritization, personalization, sequencing and measurement so the team consistently reaches the right companies at the right time Make the GTM team more productive: automate repetitive work across account research, meeting preparation, follow-ups, CRM hygiene and handoffs so BDRs, AEs and Account Managers spend more time with customers Run the revenue operating infrastructure: own the systems behind pipeline management, forecasting, funnel reporting, quota planning, GTM incentive compensation, renewals and expansion Set the rules of engagement: own account assignment and routing, settle ownership disputes, and make sure every meeting booked and held is captured and credited to the right person Improve how revenue work moves through Kernel: build reliable routing, attribution, account assignment and cross-functional handoffs, resolve edge cases and make performance visible Be Kernel's own internal customer: deploy Kernel on our CRM, use it to improve our GTM data and workflows, and turn what you learn into useful feedback for Product and Engineering What You Bring 3-5 years of relevant experience: you have worked in RevOps, Sales Ops or GTM Engineering at a high-growth Series B-E SaaS company and owned meaningful parts of the revenue engine end to end Deep Salesforce fluency: you understand objects, record types, fields, formulas, flows, validation rules, permissions, reports and data migration. You can reason about architecture and debug production behavior Strong GTM building ability: you have built useful systems with Clay, APIs, automation platforms and AI tools, and you know how to move from a rough idea to a reliable workflow that people adopt Commercial judgment: you understand how accounts become meetings, meetings become pipeline, pipeline is qualified and forecast, and won revenue flows into implementation, expansion, renewal and retention Strong data instincts: you can turn fragmented information into trustworthy workflows, measure what is working and create feedback loops that improve performance over time Clear, low-ego communication: you can turn a messy request into a crisp decision, explain trade-offs to non-technical teams, push back constructively and drive adoption through influence rather than authority It is a plus if you also have: Experience supporting an enterprise sales motion with multi-stakeholder deals and MEDDPICC Experience with renewals, expansion, compensation, quota setting or planning Familiarity with Gong, sales engagement platforms and modern enrichment or intent tooling Experience building operational controls around LLM- or agent-powered workflows ⚠️ This role may not be for you if you: Prefer strategy and recommendations over configuring systems, cleaning data, investigating edge cases and debugging workflows yourself Need outlined requirements or stable priorities before you can make progress See GTM Engineering primarily as CRM administration or ticket fulfillment rather than a revenue-generating function ❌ This role is definitely not for you if you: Are not comfortable taking broad ownership of a function Prefer a predictable, low-intensity environment Want to protect a 9-to-6 or a mostly remote setup. We are in the office together 4-5 days a week and the pace is high What We Offer We will do our best to offer you a ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling. 💰 Salary: £70,000-£90,000 + equity 🗓️ 24 days holiday per year + bank holidays 🥕 £450 monthly office dinner allowance ✈️ 2 weeks work-from-anywhere 🍼 Generous parental leave policy 💼 Pension plan 💻 Top-spec equipment and central London office 🎉 Team events and dinners 🚀 Work directly with the founders to build the systems that power an AI-native revenue engine 🏆 High-autonomy, high-trust environment with a small team shipping at pace ❤️ Team Arvin Ashrafi, Head of Finance & Operations Amin Shafi, BizOps Associate Dave Bentham, Head of Sales 🎫 Visas & Relocation Not offered for this role. title: Junior Compute Architect
description: About Fractile Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts. The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems. About the Hardware organisation at Fractile Processor Architecture sits within Fractile’s hardware organisation, which owns everything from compute engine definition and ISA design through memory hierarchies, on-chip interconnects, and the path from early architectural exploration through to tapeout and post-silicon validation. Architecture at Fractile isn’t a paper exercise — it’s built in constant collaboration with logical design, physical design, and verification teams, so that every architectural decision is grounded in what will actually perform in working silicon. About the team and role As an Early Career Processor Architect, you’ll join our architecture team to learn how to define the compute engines, ISA definitions and programming models that sit at the heart of our silicon. Working closely with senior architects and our logical design, physical design, and verification teams, you’ll get real exposure to performance modelling, specification writing, bottleneck analysis, and pre- and post-silicon validation — with experienced architects mentoring you as you build toward owning more of this yourself. About you We’re looking for someone with a strong foundational understanding of computer or processor architecture — built through coursework, personal projects, internships, placements, or research — who’s genuinely curious about performance and power trade-offs and eager to learn how to navigate them. You don’t need prior industry experience as a Processor Architect; what matters is real hands-on exposure to processor or accelerator design, through a final-year project, FPGA build, RISC-V implementation, internship, or research, plus a comfort working across disciplines and a track record of thriving in ambiguity and fast iteration. Key Requirements A degree (BEng, MEng, MSc or equivalent) in Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience. A solid foundational understanding of computer/processor architecture, including matrix- and vector-centric floating-point arithmetic and memory hierarchies, gained through study, projects, internships, or research. Some exposure to RTL design concepts and how physical design constraints feed back into architectural choices — academic or internship-level experience is fine. Any hands-on exposure to architectural performance modelling tools (gem5, SystemC, or custom cycle-accurate simulators), compiler/toolchain interactions, or AI acceleration/vector-matrix compute, through study or projects, is highly valued. A clear communicator, comfortable working across architecture, modelling, implementation, verification, and software teams, who thrives in ambiguity and fast iteration. A chain of trust from the hardware up to the rack management plane: the root of trust each controller boots from, the signed updates that reach the fleet safely, the identity that lets a device prove what it is, the authenticated channels the controllers and devices talk over, and the runtime protections that keep the host Linux kernel and the on-die firmware trustworthy long after boot. In this role, the security of your software solutions depends entirely on how well you understand the hardware beneath it. Some of the protections we rely on live in silicon, some in software, and part of the skill is knowing which belongs where. We’re looking for people who know both sides well enough to build the mechanisms that close whole classes of bugs by design. We’re not heavy on levels here! Whether you’d call yourself senior, staff, principal, or lead, what matters is depth of security judgement, system-level experience, and working well with the engineers around you. If you’ve worked deep in the security of real systems and like to get your hands on the code and the systems around it, we’d like to hear from you. If you want to architect the benchmark for trust and resilience in global finance, your work here will have a massive impact. You’ll act as an investigative subject-matter expert and operational lead, helping identify and mitigate risks across cross-border payments, corporate accounts, cards, FX and embedded finance. Deep understanding of cross-border payment mechanisms, including SWIFT, local ACH and clearing schemes, and FX; business payment flows; merchant acquiring; and corporate entity structures, including complex shareholding, shell companies and beneficial ownership. Solid working knowledge of global AML/CTF and sanctions regulatory frameworks, including, where applicable,FATF recommendations, FinCEN/BSA, FCA, AUSTRAC,MAS and other relevant local regulatory requirements. title: Engineering Manager, Guardian
description: About the Team The Guardian team builds practical safety and oversight systems for increasingly capable AI agents. Our goal is to make it possible for agents to take on longer-running, higher-autonomy work while preserving meaningful safeguards, respecting user intent, and intervening when actions could cause serious or difficult-to-reverse harm. Auto-review is an early example of this work. When an agent reaches a permission boundary, a separate model evaluates the proposed action in context and determines whether it should proceed. The team is now extending this foundation into more capable oversight systems that account for richer user context, support a broader range of agent experiences, and integrate across OpenAI products. Guardian sits at the intersection of engineering, alignment research, product, infrastructure, and security. The team already has a strong engineering foundation in London and will continue to grow there as a concentrated, highly collaborative group. About the Role We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead and grow the Guardian team in London. You will own the engineering strategy and execution for production systems that evaluate agent behavior, identify risk, and take appropriate action without creating unnecessary friction for users. This is a builder-manager role with substantial technical depth. You will set direction, develop engineers, and create the operating cadence for a high-performing team, while remaining close enough to the work to shape architecture, review designs, debug difficult problems, and write code when it is the highest-leverage way to help the team move forward. The role is highly visible and cross-functional. You will work closely with alignment researchers to translate emerging research into dependable systems, and with product teams to make agent safety a foundational capability across OpenAI. This role is based in our London office. In this role, you will Lead, hire, and develop a London-based team of engineers working across agent safety, backend systems, applied AI, and product infrastructure. Set the technical roadmap for Auto-review and the broader Guardian platform, balancing safety, product utility, latency, and operational reliability. Build production systems that evaluate agent actions in real time, detect potentially harmful behavior, and support safe recovery or escalation paths. Improve how oversight systems understand user intent, environmental context, permissions, and relevant personalization signals while protecting privacy and avoiding unnecessary friction. Partner closely with alignment researchers to turn prototypes, evaluations, and new monitoring techniques into scalable product capabilities. Work across Product, Security, Infrastructure, and other engineering teams to integrate Guardian capabilities into agent experiences throughout OpenAI. Establish rigorous evaluation and operational practices, including adversarial testing, failure analysis, monitoring, and metrics for safety performance, false positives, latency, and user impact. You might thrive in this role if you Have significant experience leading engineering teams that shipped complex, high-stakes production systems end to end. Have built with AI agents or large language models in a core product, startup, or technically serious independent project, and understand the unique challenges of agentic systems. Bring strong product-engineering judgment and can navigate tradeoffs across safety, usability, speed, and reliability. Can partner effectively with research teams, translate open-ended findings into engineering plans, and communicate clearly across technical disciplines. Have a thoughtful management system for hiring, coaching, performance, and execution. Care deeply about building AI systems that are useful, trustworthy, and safe. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. title: Senior Hub Developer
description: We're looking for a developer to grow Ember's network of charging hubs. You'll find the sites, take them through legals and planning, manage the build and energise them. How you work and think matters more to us than which industry you've worked in. You think clearly, can run several projects at once and are as at home on a site as behind a desk. About Ember We're building the future of public transport — convenient, affordable, connected and zero-emission. Our goal is to make it easier and more enjoyable to get from A to B with Ember than it is with your own car. Ember is a tech company, not a traditional bus operator. We've built a platform that coordinates our entire operation — everything from monitoring vehicles and controlling chargers to selling tickets and calculating ETAs. This allows us to use electric buses more intensively than anyone else in the world, leading to a massive reduction in emissions. It also helps us provide a much better passenger experience, with innovative features like demand-responsive stops. We’re still tiny, with a handful of routes and ~100 buses. The challenge is to scale this 50x whilst staying lean, increasing efficiency and delivering an even better product experience. We’ve recently raised a Series A from some of Europe’s leading climate VCs and are looking for mission-driven individuals who want to get on board and help take us to the next level. The role Charging hubs are Ember's key growth enabler. They give us the ultra-fast charge points we need to run our network, and they act as a base for our fleet — parking, washing, driver lounges and more. We have hubs across Scotland today, with additional sites across the UK under construction or in the pipeline. You'll join a small team of four, taking end-to-end responsibility for your own sites and helping out on others. We're typically running a handful of projects at any one time. Step one is finding a site. You’ll need to think about where we need charging capacity to support future routes, scout industrial estates and brownfield plots and reach out to commercial agents, local authorities and landlords. Some great sites are advertised but many are not, so landing one usually means being patient and creative. Once you've got a site, we move on to lease negotiations, design, the planning application and the power connection. You'll work with network operators to land the grid connection, and with our suppliers to procure, install and commission the charging equipment. Solicitors, architects and engineers are there to help, but the project is yours to drive — you set the direction, you ask the difficult questions and you make the trade-offs. It’s important to be hands-on. We don't go to tender and leave the rest to an outsourced project manager — we want you on site, asking why a kerb is in the wrong place. Even after a site is live, our involvement doesn't stop. The team keeps refining and improving every site, and you'll be part of that work across the network, not just on the sites you've built yourself. Diversity and equality At Ember, we support diversity across our team and customers. We work to ensure every employee feels respected and able to give their best, whether temporary, part-time or full-time. We’re happy to offer flexible working patterns where they make sense, are compassionate when it comes to time off and offer enhanced maternity and paternity leave. Read more about our approach in our Equal Opportunities Policy . What's on offer You'll receive a salary of £50,000–£75,000 per annum, depending on your experience and skills, plus share options. You'll be expected to work from our lovely office in central Edinburgh most days — we value in-person communication — but there's flexibility around the odd day from home, with an expectation that you'll spend some time travelling to different sites. How do I apply? Send your CV and a short note on why this interests you. Applications close Friday 27 November at 5pm. Who we're looking for You should have a desire to get involved in the growth of a quickly scaling business, with a real opportunity to make your mark. How you work and think matters more to us than specific industry experience. The following should sound a lot like you: Curious and quick to learn. You're comfortable in unfamiliar territory — new technical specs, new legal terms, new planning processes — and you treat each one as an opportunity to learn. You don't expect to know everything on day one. Engineering mindset. You're the sort of person who'll happily watch YouTube videos explaining concrete reinforcement, three-phase distribution or substation transformers. You'll be excited to dive into the same level of detail on our projects. A first-principles thinker. You take problems back to fundamentals rather than reaching for jargon or the way things are usually done. When you work with experts — solicitors, architects, engineers — you treat them as people you can learn from, not people you can outsource your thinking to. Commercially astute. You can tell when something is worth fighting for and when it's better to redesign around a constraint, whether that's a lease, a planning condition or a contractor's quote. Highly organised. Managing a pipeline of projects is complex, with many timelines, people to chase, details to look into and things that can (and will) go wrong. We want you at Inbox Zero, not in inbox hell. Comfortable using AI. At a minimum you use it as part of how you work — to learn faster, draft documents and get to the bottom of unfamiliar topics. But maybe you’ll go further and build software to help the team work faster and more precisely. Hands-on. Hubs are built in the real world, not behind a screen. You'll meet landlords, talk to electricians and look at drains, but you'll also need to read contracts and chase agents who've gone quiet. A strong sense of what good looks like. Whatever the topic, problem or issue. You need to know how to hold yourself and others to a high standard. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Staff Analytics Engineer
description: About Pleo Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’. The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years. Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role This is a senior individual contributor role in our Data Services & Governance team where you'll act as the thought and technical leader owning the semantic layer and analytics standards for Pleo. This means that you won't own a domain but you'll own what good looks like across all of them by developing, improving , maintaining and evangelising our modelling standards and AI-augmented development practices that every Analytics Engineer work with, regardless of which team they sit in. The semantic layer you will be designing and maintaining will be the single source of truth that AI agents, BI tools, and analysts query. This is foundational work with company-wide reach which will be ideal for you if you enjoy building things from the ground up. Our semantic layer is still in very early stage. Tooling selection is live, and this role has a strong voice in it. Our BI stack is also in transition so, you would not be inheriting a mature setup and maintaining it. You'd be deciding what it should be, then building it. For additional context, our tech stack currently include: GCP, BigQuery, dbt Core, Airflow, SQL, Python, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot. Who you'll work with You'll report to the Data Engineering Manager who oversees the Data Infra & MLOps team as well as the Data Services & Governance team. Your primary relationship will be with Analytics Engineers embedded across the Intelligence function who should come to you for architecture guidance, semantic layer decisions, and standards questions. You will also partner with a Staff Data Engineer on data engineering standards and pipeline practices, and with others on self-serve analytics and BI tooling governance. You'll engage with the Data Serving team on entity definitions and with the GenAI Platform team on what AI-ready data looks like at the platform boundary. What you'll be doing Own the semantic layer: define what a metric definition is, how it's structured, where it lives, and how it's enforced. The goal is one canonical definition of Monthly recurring revenue (MRR), churn, transaction, customer - used by analysts, BI tools, and AI tools without divergence. You make that real, not aspirational. Set data modelling standards for the function: what clean, layered, well-tested dbt architecture looks like across all domains, at all levels of complexity. Build and run the Analytics Engineering community of practice including code reviews, shared patterns, documentation, onboarding etc. The goal is to create a social infrastructure that makes standards stick. Own the AI-native development practice. Use AI coding tools as a native part of how you write, review, and migrate data models (not as a demonstration, but as your actual workflow). Evaluate what works in a governed data engineering context, what introduces risk, and shape how the Analytics Engineering community adopts it. Lead responsible AI-augmented migration work using AI tooling to accelerate data modelling and migrations across the Analytics Warehouse and Operational Data Platform. Design data models and metric definitions in a documented and structured manner enabling reliable consumption by AI services without human intervention. Engage upstream with backend and product engineers to drive data contract discipline and schema ownership upstream, rather than managing inconsistency downstream. Contribute to Data & AI Products for external customer-facing analytics where data modelling patterns and conversational analytics needs and capabilities grow. What you bring Deep demonstrated expertise in dbt and modelling practices: not just strong modelling, but a formed view of what modelling architecture should look like across a function. You can defend trade-offs, teach them, and enforce them in teams you don't manage. Deep BigQuery and SQL expertise, including performance, cost considerations, and the architectural challenges of complex analytical domains. Real experience owning a semantic layer (LookML, dbt MetricFlow, or equivalent). You have a point of view on what metric consistency should look like at scale, what breaks when it doesn't, and how to design it so AI tooling can consume it without degrading trust. AI-native development practice in a data engineering context. You use AI coding tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent) as a genuine part of how you work, and you can be specific about where they add real value and where they introduce risk in a governed analytics codebase. A track record of setting standards across teams you don't directly manage and making them stick by leveraging effective influencing techniques as opposed to relying on authority. Understanding of what LLMs and agentic tools need from a data layer such as how to model data, write documentation, and define metrics so that AI tools get consistent answers at runtime. Proven experience engaging credibly with backend engineers on data contracts and with senior stakeholders on what the semantic layer strategy means for the business. Why this role is a good fit for you This role is a good fit if: You can hold a standard without needing it applied perfectly, and you know which compromises are fatal and which are just untidy. You genuinely enjoy growing a community of practice through influence rather than authority and you take pride in seeing colleagues adopt and grow standards. You find the "how do we make data legible to an agent, not just to an analyst" problem interesting in its own right, rather than as a trend to keep up with. This role is not a good fit if You want to own a domain. The Intelligence teams have strong AEs doing that. This role is for someone who wants to own the standards they build to. You advise others to use AI coding tools but don't use them yourself. AI-native development is part of the mandate, not a differentiating nice-to-have. You are more comfortable being consulted than being accountable. The semantic layer and modelling standards you set have downstream consequences across the whole function and in AI features customers use. Your first 6 months By the end of your first six months, you'll have: Mapped the current state of modelling standards and the semantic layer across the function (where definitions are consistent, where they diverge, and what the highest-impact gaps are) to draft a plan the function has bought into. Contributed to the semantic layer tooling decision and begun onboarding the Analytics Engineers who'll build to it by writing documentation, running live sessions, reviewing PRs etc. Established a visible presence in the AE community of practice and become someone whose feedback in code reviews and whose opinions on architecture are listened to because they've been demonstrated, not just stated. Run your own workflow on AI coding tooling to the point where you can say clearly what the function should adopt, what it should not, and why. The interview process We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows: Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background. Core skills test: A technical test you'll be taking through an external platform to showcase your grasp of analytics engineering fundamentals. Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute conversation-based interview aimed at deep diving into your previous experience and learning more about the team. Pleo Challenge: A live practical and technical interview designed to assess your problem solving skills as well as your technical expertise. Final interview: A 45-minutes interview with one of our senior leaders, focusing on assessing behavioural skills and values alignment. Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application: We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you—not AI—know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background. Every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process. This is a Staff level role at Pleo. This means it's a very senior position where you need to demonstrate experience leading technical initiatives that can have organisation-wide or cross-team impact for a tech business of 500-1000+ people. title: Revenue Operations Manager
description: About Us Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact. We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem . Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work. At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. The Role We're looking for a Revenue Operations Manager to join our Revenue Operations team and act as a broad, senior partner to our revenue organization. You'll set and execute the strategy for how we build revenue analytics across Salesforce and Looker, run insights that shape how revenue leadership sees the business, partner closely with revenue leadership on the full range of topics they face, and, as you ramp up, take on growing ownership of the forecasting cadence alongside the Director of Revenue Operations. This is a generalist role by design: analytics is the foundation, especially in your first two quarters, and the role broadens from there to include business partnering and forecasting. What matters most is the versatility to move across all three, not depth in any single one. What You'll Do First 90 days: Scope the revenue analytics strategy and build the core dashboards. First 180 days: Build a highly automated revenue insights engine using AI, while establishing yourself as the business partner revenue leadership. First 12 months: Broaden into leading and supporting the forecasting cadence. What Will You Be Doing? Revenue Analytics & Insights Partner with the Director of Revenue Operations to define the revenue analytics strategy: what we need to build across Salesforce and Looker, and in what order. Map the current reporting landscape — what exists, what's trusted, what's duplicated or out of date — and use that map to shape the build plan. Own execution of that plan: build and maintain the core dashboards and reports that revenue leadership and the wider revenue leadership team rely on. Launch and run a recurring insights digest for revenue leaders, turning dashboards and data into a clear narrative — what changed, why it matters, what to do about it. Bring a point of view on what's worth building versus what's noise, and be willing to push back on requests that don't earn their keep. Business Partnership to Revenue leadership Become the go-to Revenue Operations partner for revenue leadership, covering reporting, insights, and the broader range of topics that come up in running a sales organization. Translate revenue leadership's open questions into structured analysis and clear, actionable recommendations. Represent revenue's priorities into the Revenue Operations roadmap, and vice versa. Support revenue leaders in business reviews, planning moments, and ad hoc requests with credible, fast turnaround. Forecasting Run the forecasting cadence with sales leaders alongside the Director of Revenue Operations — forecast calls, pipeline reviews, and accuracy tracking. Build and refine forecasting models based on pipeline, productivity, and historical conversion. Conduct strategic analyses to determine forecasting trends and identify opportunities for process improvement. What Will You Need to Succeed? 5+ years of experience in Revenue or Sales Operations, preferably in a SaaS or technology company operating at a global or European level. Exposure to Account Executive (AE) or similarly quota-carrying organization. Strong Salesforce reporting skills and working fluency in a BI tool (Looker or equivalent), with a practical, business-first approach to data. A genuine generalist mindset — as comfortable building a dashboard or an insights report, as running a forecasting call. A track record of setting direction and quality bar for analytical work. Strong stakeholder management, with the ability to work with and influence sales leadership and revenue executives. Comfortable owning ambiguous problems end to end: framing the question, choosing the method, landing the recommendation. Excellent written communication — the insights digest is a core, ongoing deliverable of this role. Experience partnering with global or multi-region teams is a plus. What we Offer Receive competitive compensation and equity ownership in Perk Rest and recharge with 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays Take control of your physical health with private medical cover and voluntary dental insurance from Bupa, and discounted gym memberships with GymFlex Plan for your future with our qualifying earnings company pension plan with Aviva Know that your loved ones are protected financially through your Life Insurance if the worst were to happen Rest assured that you’re covered by income protection in case you experience a long-term sickness or absence Leverage tax-efficient cycle and electric car schemes with Cycle2Work & Octopus Join our unforgettable Perk events, including our spectacular annual summer party Always feel supported with Spring Health, our market-leading wellbeing partner, providing fast, comprehensive access to 12x therapy and 12x coaching sessions for you and your loved ones Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave Contribute to your community with 16 paid hours per year to spend volunteering for your dearest charitable causes Broaden your horizons with up to 20 "Work from Anywhere" days per year Stay savvy with access to a wide variety of discounts and rewards Follow your passions and take a four-week, fully paid sabbatical once you reach 5 years Let us help you move to one of our hubs with relocation support AI at Perk AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes. How We Work At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work. For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume. Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. title: Technical Architect
description: <p><strong>ABOUT NEXGEN CLOUD</strong></p> <p>NexGen Cloud is a fast-growing GPU cloud and AI infrastructure business. We’re the company behind Hyperstack — a self-serve, on-demand cloud platform built for high-performance AI, HPC, and compute-heavy workloads. Powered by 100% renewable energy and NVIDIA architecture, Hyperstack gives teams from AI startups to enterprise the compute they need, without the cost or complexity of legacy cloud.</p> <p>We move fast, solve hard problems, and build things that matter. If you want ownership, real impact, and a front-row seat to one of the most consequential infrastructure shifts of the decade — this is the place.</p> <p><strong>THE ROLE: Technical Architect</strong></p> <p>We’re deploying large-scale NVIDIA GPU clusters, including GB200 and GB300 rack-scale systems, into live data centres on tight customer commit dates. On those schedules, a design error found on site costs weeks and real money. We need one architect per deployment who takes the high-level design and turns it into something that can actually be built, then stays with it until the customer signs off.</p> <p>This is a role for someone who would rather find the problem on paper than on the data hall floor. It suits someone who will push back on an inherited design or a customer requirement that won’t perform, and who carries authority through owning the design rather than managing people.</p> <p><strong>WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING</strong></p> <p>Rather than a checklist, here’s what success in this role actually looks like:</p> <ul> <li>Take each cluster from CTO handover to customer acceptance as its single design authority, so nothing is ordered or installed against a design you haven’t validated</li> <li>Turn high-level designs and initial BOMs into build-ready low-level designs, hall layouts, rack elevations, P2P maps and cable schedules that site teams can build from without having to call you</li> <li>Design the InfiniBand and Ethernet fabric, power, direct liquid cooling and containment to fit the real constraints of each data centre</li> <li>Validate every BOM before it goes to procurement, and make part substitution calls knowing exactly what breaks when a line changes</li> <li>Hold OEMs and integrators (NVIDIA, Dell, Lenovo, Supermicro and others) to their technical commitments, from FAT witness through to on-site issue resolution</li> <li>Build the reference designs and building blocks that mean each new deployment starts from a known-good baseline rather than a blank page</li> </ul> <p><strong>ABOUT YOU</strong></p> <p>We care more about how you think and work than a perfect CV. You’ll likely bring a combination of the following:</p> <p><em>Essential:</em></p> <ul> <li>You’ve designed and delivered large-scale GPU or HPC clusters into live data centres, and you were on site for the build</li> <li>Deep, practical knowledge of NVIDIA platforms (GB200/GB300 rack-scale and HGX H200/B200) and what each one demands of a facility</li> <li>Cluster-scale InfiniBand and Ethernet fabric design: topology, rail optimisation, oversubscription, and cable and optic selection</li> <li>Physical infrastructure design across power and redundancy, direct liquid cooling and CDUs, containment and achievable cable lengths</li> <li>You know part numbers, what’s optional and what isn’t, and you can hold an OEM to account when their commitments slip</li> </ul> <p><em>Nice to Have:</em></p> <ul> <li>Factory integration and FAT experience, including holding a dispatch gate</li> <li>Storage design for AI workloads (WEKA, VAST, DDN, Ceph or similar)</li> <li>Deployments across multiple geographies and data centre operators, including sites requiring fit-out</li> <li>Neocloud or hyperscale experience on compressed schedules</li> </ul> <p><strong>WHAT WE OFFER</strong></p> <ul> <li>Competitive salary and annual discretionary bonus scheme</li> <li>Employee wellbeing benefits</li> <li>25 days holiday, plus public holidays</li> <li>Private Medical Insurance</li> <li>Enhanced Pension Scheme</li> <li>Flexible working arrangements (remote or hybrid, depending on role and location)</li> <li>Real ownership and autonomy — the trust to take initiative and experiment</li> <li>Visible, meaningful impact as we scale</li> <li>Clear career progression in a high-growth company</li> <li>A collaborative, international culture built on trust, transparency, and ownership</li> <li>The chance to help shape NexGen Cloud’s team, culture, and future</li> </ul> <p><strong>WHY APPLY</strong></p> <p>We welcome applications from all backgrounds. If you enjoy solving complex infrastructure problems and want to build something meaningful at scale, we’d like to hear from you.</p> <p><strong>MORE INFORMATION</strong></p> <p>Visit our <a href="https://www.nexgencloud.com/careers">careers page</a> to learn more about us or follow us on <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/nexgen-cloud">LinkedIn</a> and <a href="https://x.com/CloudNexgen">X</a> to learn more about our journey and keep up with our latest news and releases.</p> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Deployment Strategist SAP & ERP Specialist
description: TL;DR You know how to walk into an enterprise, spot the pain points in its ERP processes, and see what good could look like. At Conduct you turn that into a game changing moment: you show leadership, with confidence, how Conduct will transform the way they run SAP. You own optimising the delivery of transformation projects with Conduct, from the first use case to adoption across the business. You build the trust that turns a pilot into a long-term partnership, and the product insights you bring back directly shape what we build next. Why Conduct The world's largest companies should move at the speed of their ideas, not the speed of the systems they run on. Today they don't, and you've seen why firsthand. Every new product line, pricing change or process redesign runs into SAP estates layered with decades of custom code, user exits and enhancements no single person fully understands. Requirements take months to ship. S/4HANA migrations cost $100M+ and years of pain, and the 2027 ECC deadline is forcing every large enterprise to face it. We're building the AI operating system that absorbs this complexity and gives enterprises back their speed. Major enterprises already trust us with their most critical systems. We've closed game-changing SI partnerships, just raised a $60M Series A, and demand is outpacing what we can service. We're a small, talent-dense team doing our life's work out of London and NYC. Extreme ownership, high velocity, low-ego collaboration. What you build here shapes the company and how the world's largest companies operate. We sponsor visas and are convinced diverse teams build better products, so we especially encourage underrepresented groups in tech to reach out. What you'll own You will make sure Conduct lands and sticks inside our most strategic SAP customers. You join accounts early, shape how Conduct fits into their transformation programmes, and fully take over post-sale. You'll have a direct line from what you see in the field to what ships in the product. Be the SAP brain in the room. Translate between CIOs, process owners, Basis teams and our engineers. Scope use cases across finance, supply chain, procurement and sales that land real value fast. Design the transformation. Get under the skin of complex, heavily customised ECC and S/4HANA landscapes. Conceptualise where Conduct can have the biggest impact, then lead the deployment that gets the customer there. Turn pilots into partnerships. Onboard hundreds of end users, prove ROI, spot expansion signals and hold the early commercial conversations that grow an account. Shape the product. You'll have a direct line into product and engineering. Your view of how SAP actually runs in the real world will shape our roadmap. Build the engine. Our GTM team is small and lean. You'll build the onboarding flows, tooling and reusable playbooks that let customer capacity compound without headcount growing linearly. Work with our SI partners. You speak their language. Help partners deploy Conduct inside their own programmes. No two days look the same. You'll fly out to customers when it counts and spend the rest of the time building alongside the team. Who we hire We're looking for people obsessed with delivering for customers. You'll fit right in if former colleagues would, without hesitating, call you one of the sharpest people they've worked with. In practice that tends to look like: 3+ years in SAP or ERP consulting , at a Big Four firm, a global SI or a specialist SAP partner. You've been on live implementations, rollouts or S/4HANA transformations, not just advisory. Real depth in at least one area of SAP. Functional (FI/CO, SD, MM, PP, EWM), technical (ABAP, integration, BTP) or solution architecture. You understand how processes and custom code fit together across the landscape. Client-facing confidence. You've run workshops, owned a workstream and earned the trust of senior stakeholders who were sceptical at first. Commercial instinct. You notice the next problem worth solving, and you understand that a great deployment is how accounts grow. Builder energy. You want to do the hands-on customer work and build the process behind it. Ambiguity excites you more than it worries you. Curiosity about AI. You don't need to be an engineer. You do need to want to learn how it works and where it breaks. Low ego, high self-awareness. You're comfortable saying "I don't know" in a complex technical room, then going and figuring it out. Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We care more about trajectory and sharpness than a perfect match. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: <p>This is an opportunity to kickstart your career by joining Canonical. From problem qualification to full resolution, you will own and manage your cases. When needed, you will transfer your cases to your colleagues or involve senior engineers. If you have an affinity for open source development and a passion for technology, then you will enjoy working with some of the best people in the industry at Canonical.</p> <p>Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1100+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.</p> <p>The company is founder led, profitable and growing.</p> <p>While our engineers regularly solve deeply interesting, complex technical problems - from triaging cloud environments to root-cause analysis on unseen Linux kernel crashes - this is fundamentally a role rooted in human connection. You will act as a trusted peer and technical guide to external engineering teams, translating intricate open-source challenges into clear, empathetic solutions. We are rapidly expanding and looking for brilliant problem solvers who are just as passionate about building strong, collaborative relationships with customers as they are about the next generation of Canonical solutions.</p> <p>Location: Office Based in London, England.</p> <h2><strong>The role entails</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Empathetic Engagement:</strong> Partner directly with customers across remote sessions, ticketing,, and live conversations to deeply understand and resolve their technical roadblocks.</li> <li><strong>Collaborative Problem Solving:</strong> Work hand-in-hand with internal engineering teams and regional peer groups to bridge the gap between complex code fixes and real-world customer satisfaction.</li> <li><strong>True Ownership:</strong> Manage your support cases with a strong sense of personal integrity, ensuring commitments are honored and customer expectations are communicated transparently and predictably.</li> <li><strong>Ubuntu Lifecycle Guidance:</strong> Develop a rich understanding of the Ubuntu development process, empowering you to give customers clear, human context regarding timelines for engineering fixes.</li> <li><strong>Knowledge Advocacy:</strong> Author and maintain accessible knowledge base articles, ensuring lessons learned are shared openly to elevate the entire open-source community.</li> <li><strong>Operational Reliability:</strong> Participate in a regular weekend working rotation to maintain seamless, high-touch continuity of care for our global partners.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What are we looking for in you</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Communication Excellence:</strong> Exceptional written and spoken English, with a natural ability to convey technical complexity clearly, warmly, and compellingly.</li> <li><strong>The Soft-Skill Edge:</strong> A genuine passion for helping people, paired with the emotional intelligence to navigate high-stakes technical situations with composure and empathy.</li> <li><strong>Academic Dedication:</strong> Exceptional academic track record from both high school and university.</li> <li><strong>Educational Background:</strong> An undergraduate degree in a technical subject or a compelling narrative about your alternative chosen path.</li> <li><strong>On-Site Technical Leadership:</strong> Based in our state-of-the-art London, UK office, you will serve as a key technical support resource for our local teams and employees.</li> <li><strong>Driven Mindset:</strong> A proven track record of going above-and-beyond expectations to deliver meaningful, outstanding results for teams or customers.</li> <li><strong>Linux & Cloud Familiarity:</strong> Practical, hands-on experience supporting Linux systems, with an exposure to three or more of the following:</li> <ul> <li><em>Virtualization & Cloud:</em> Using KVM or OpenStack.</li> <li><em>Containers:</em> primarily Docker, LXD/LXC, or Kubernetes.</li> <li><em>Storage Ecosystems:</em> Block, object, and network storage technologies.</li> <li><em>System Networking:</em> Navigating bonding, firewalls, bridging, switching, or MTU tuning.</li> </ul> <li><strong>Analytical Curiosity:</strong> A strong troubleshooting mindset—the ability to look into stack traces or logs, identify OS/application-level bugs, and strategically guide the customer through next steps.</li> <li><strong>Development Fundamentals:</strong> Basic programming logic in any language to help parse code and collaborate effectively with Canonical Engineering teams.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What we offer colleagues</strong></h2> <p>We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.</p> <ul> <li>Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person</li> <li>Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year</li> <li>Annual compensation review</li> <li>Recognition rewards</li> <li>Annual holiday leave</li> <li>Maternity and paternity leave</li> <li>Employee Assistance Programme</li> <li>Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues</li> <li>Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About Canonical</strong></h3> <p>Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.</p> <p><strong>Canonical is an equal opportunity employer</strong></p> <p>We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. title: Support Engineer
description: <p>Accelerate your technical career by joining Canonical in a high-impact, multi-disciplinary role.. You'll be working from our London office, which hosts our events, customer demos and visitors, in an event space with professional live video, audio and streaming equipment. You'll wear three hats: Linux and cloud support engineer, owner of the office's technical infrastructure, and one of the people running the live production at our events. You'll own your cases from first contact to resolution, bringing in colleagues or senior engineers when needed, and you'll keep the technology running when it matters most, with people watching. While professional broadcast or AV experience is not required, a strong technical curiosity for audio/video systems and the composure to manage live, high-stakes environments are a must.</p> <p>Location: Office Based in London, England.</p> <p><strong>The role entails</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Office technology:</strong> Own the technical state of the London office (network, devices, meeting spaces, AV), including onboarding new colleagues, and know how it all fits together.</li> <li><strong>Live events:</strong> Run the technology for events and customer demos, from set-up and live operation through to tear-down, and coordinate external crew for larger events.</li> <li><strong>Customer support:</strong> Own your cases end to end, working with customers by ticket, remote session and live conversation, and with engineering teams to turn code fixes into customer outcomes. Set clear expectations and keep your commitments.</li> <li><strong>Ubuntu lifecycle:</strong> Understand the Ubuntu development process well enough to give customers realistic timelines for fixes.</li> <li><strong>Knowledge:</strong> Write and maintain knowledge base articles so lessons learned are shared.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What are we looking for in you</strong></p> <ul> <li>Exceptional written and spoken English, and the ability to explain technical complexity clearly and warmly</li> <li>An exceptional academic record at high school and university, with an undergraduate degree in a technical subject or a compelling narrative about your alternative path</li> <li>A builder's streak: something you've set up or run for other people on a deadline, such as a home lab, hackspace, student tech crew, live sound, streaming, or school or club IT</li> <li>AV curiosity: real interest in audio, video and live production, or a clear appetite to learn it </li> <li>Composure and care: you like helping people and stay calm when a high-stakes moment, including a live event, gets tense</li> <li>A track record of going above and beyond for teams or customers</li> <li>Hands-on experience supporting Linux systems, plus any of: virtualization or cloud (KVM, OpenStack), containers (Docker, LXD/LXC, Kubernetes), storage (block, object, network), or networking (bonding, firewalls, bridging, switching, MTU tuning)</li> <li>A troubleshooting mindset (logs, stack traces, OS and application-level causes) and programming fundamentals in any language</li> </ul> <p><strong>What we offer colleagues</strong></p> <p>We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We assess performance and revisit compensation twice annually to ensure we recognize outstanding colleagues. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.</p> <ul> <li>Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person.</li> <li>Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year.</li> <li>Bi-annual compensation review.</li> <li>Company recognition rewards.</li> <li>40 days annual leave per annum, including public holidays and our All Company holiday periods.</li> <li>Maternity and paternity leave.</li> <li>Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform.</li> <li>Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues, with Priority Pass for lounge access.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About Canonical</strong></p> <p>Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. We are founder-led, profitable, and growing.</p> <p>Powered by worldwide distributed collaboration since our inception in 2004, we believe tech and business leadership can emerge anywhere. We have no central headquarters. Most of us work from home, but we are exceptionally disciplined about this. We have very high expectations of all colleagues, and are champions of excellence. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.</p> <p><strong>Canonical is an equal opportunity employer</strong></p> <p>We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. <a href="https://canonical.com/careers/diversity/identity">Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.</a></p>

title: Lead Product Manager, Growth
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/personal">personal</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/business-banking">business</a> bank accounts, we offer <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/joint-account">joint accounts</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/16-17">accounts for 16-17 year olds</a>, a <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/under-16s">free kids account</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/flex">credit cards</a> in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. This is a rare opportunity to lead one of Monzo’s most strategically critical product domains, owning high-complexity bets that shape how millions of people discover, join and trust our bank.</p> <p>You will own the strategic direction across our core growth engines: how we attract, onboard and activate people from their very first interaction. For our team, this means optimising the entire sign-up experience, removing activation friction, designing seamless new user journeys, and building powerful referral loops that turn everyday banking utility into organic network effects.</p> <p>You’ll set a compelling multi-cycle vision, craft multiple high-signal strategies, and create the experimentation engine that turns ambition into reality. We’re looking for someone who pairs an analyst's data rigour with world-class product craft, and possesses the conviction to make non-obvious bets without precedent.<br><br></p> <p><strong>🔑You’ll play a key role by...<br><br></strong></p> <ul> <li>Leading the charge: set a durable product vision and strategy that spans multiple cycles, ensuring alignment with Monzo’s goals and an exceptional customer experience.</li> <li>Communicating effectively: you get people inspired by the product vision and you share the right context with the right people at the right time.</li> <li>Collaborating seamlessly: lead through influence across collectives, building deep partnerships with engineering, design, data, fincrime, legal and marketing to resolve complex organisational trade-offs.</li> <li>Delivering impact: define, deliver and measure the impact of the customer-focused experiences you create.</li> <li>Establishing high-velocity operating rhythms that empower squads to switch seamlessly between rapid experimentation, deep iteration and bold 0-1 builds.<br><br></li> </ul> <p><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…</strong></p> <ul> <li>You are a seasoned growth product manager, and have led multiple high-performing teams to ship world-class products at a fast growing company.</li> <li>You have a track record of leading high-scale consumer growth efforts that drive significant top of funnel value for customers and scaling for the business. </li> <li>You're exceptionally data-driven and commercial, and you know when to lean on rapid experimentation and when to move quicker with high conviction from first principles.</li> <li>You can systematically break down high-ambiguity product spaces that lack precedent, structuring clear narratives that cut through noise and align teams.</li> <li>You have excellent judgement, and have a track record of making good decisions in complex situations where there’s often no “right answer”. </li> <li>You hold an uncompromising standard for product craft, moving effortlessly between high level company strategy and deep execution.</li> <li>You can work effectively with a diverse range of people and working styles - spanning engineering, design, data, user research, marketing, legal and compliance - to get stuff done.</li> <li>You’re a great storyteller, who is able to motivate, energise and inspire people towards a common goal.</li> <li>You have experience mentoring, coaching or managing other product managers, setting a high performance bar and multiplying your impact through the people around you.</li> </ul> <p>Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! Studies show that women and people of colour might hesitate to apply unless they meet every single requirement. At Monzo, we’re dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming team. If you’re passionate about this role and keen to learn and grow with us, we encourage you to apply— even if you don’t have everything that's listed just yet. Drop us your application, we’d love to hear from you!</p> <p><strong>🙌 What’s in it for you</strong></p> <p>💰 £120,000 - £140,000 ➕ Incentive Awards tied to your performance.</p> <p>✈️ We’ll help you relocate to the UK.</p> <p>✅ We can sponsor your visa. </p> <p>📍This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London)</p> <p>⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team. </p> <p>📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.</p> <p>🏡 We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given Macbooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup. </p> <p>➕ Plus lots more! <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">Read our full list of benefits</a>.</p> <p><br><br></p> <p><strong>🌈</strong><strong> The application journey has 3 key steps</strong></p> <p><br><strong>First stage - Recruiter screen<br></strong><strong>Second stage - Meet with our PM team<br></strong><strong>Third stage - Product full loop</strong></p> <p>This process should take around 3-4 weeks - your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible! </p> <p>We have some guidelines on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to ace an application and interview at Monzo. <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/the-ultimate-guide-on-using-ai-to-ace-an-interview-at-monzo">You can read them here.</a></p> <p>We’ll only close this role once we have enough applications for the next stage. We work alongside our first line credit teams who design the products, decide who to lend to, set underwriting policy, identify customers who need help, manage the portfolio and report and measure credit risk.</p> <p>Within CIF, we are scaling up our Forecasting modelling and execution team to support the enhancement of modelling standards across Finance. The role holder will have the opportunity to lead a ‘consultancy style’ centre of excellence providing thought leadership on the methodological design and regulatory compliance assessment on all Financial forecasting models that feed the banks’ budgeting and stress-testing activities. This will expand to hands-on delivery of model developments, where appropriate. </p> <p>Strong data and analytical skills are a must, as is experience in financial modelling and coding (Python and SQL preferred). Experience working in regulatory stress testing exercises (such as ICAAP or EBA Stress-testing) is highly desirable but not essential. </p> <p>We rely heavily on the following tools and technologies (note we do not expect applicants to have prior experience of all them):</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/">Google Cloud Platform</a> for all of our analytics infrastructure</li> <li><a href="https://www.getdbt.com/">dbt</a> and<a href="https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/"><strong> </strong>BigQuery SQL</a> for our data modelling and warehousing</li> <li>Python for data science and predictive modelling and data visualisation (via streamlit)</li> <li>Anaplan for model implementation</li> <li>Github for version control</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>🔑 You’ll play a key role by...</strong></p> <ul> <li>Assisting with continuous improvement of forecasting models via individual delivery or through others</li> <li>Development of best practices for financial modelling across Monzo</li> <li>Presenting forecast model results to senior management</li> <li>Close collaboration with portfolio strategy, model validation, finance and external audit teams</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…</strong></p> <ul> <li>You have a background in financial forecast modelling or execution</li> <li>You have strong analytical skills and a track record of using these to deliver technical projects</li> <li>You have a solid technical toolkit. SQL and Python are our desired coding languages but experience in SAS/R will be considered. title: Sales Account Executive
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. Our UK customers can also <a href="https://monzo.com/savings">save</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/investments">invest </a>and <a href="https://monzo.com/pensions">combine their pensions</a> with us. </p> <p>With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!</p> <p>We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️</p> <hr> <p> </p></div><p>📍London | 💰£67,000 Total OTE (base salary + commission) <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">Benefits</a> | <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U62l09nB0M4">Hear from the team</a> ✨<strong><br><br></strong></p> <p><strong>⭐ About our Business Banking Sales team</strong></p> <p>We are rapidly growing and now serve over 730,000 businesses in the UK 🇬🇧</p> <p>In order to support the next phase of our expansion, we’re hiring a small team of experienced <strong>Sales Account Executives</strong>, whose mission is to reach out and support more complex high value customers with a personalised experience. </p> <p>We’re building an acquisition engine and your job will be to work with small-medium business (SMB) prospective customers, guide them through their buying journey, work with them to activate their account and bring all their banking needs to Monzo. </p> <p>This is an exciting opportunity to be a part of the founding sales team for a mission driven company , which is changing how people and businesses bank. </p> <p><strong>🔑 You’ll play a key role by…</strong></p> <ul> <li>Engaging with prospective SMB customers through discovery calls, and understand their business, challenges, goals and requirements.</li> <li>Driving full sales cycle, from early prospecting and qualification; to demos and sales;  to ensuring successful account switch and activation.</li> <li>Guiding customers through Monzo’s business banking offerings - providing clear, factual information and helping them evaluate what works best.</li> <li>Being a product expert: fully understand Monzo's business banking products, features and services.</li> <li>Managing a pipeline of leads with strong attention to data hygiene: timely follow-ups, accurate forecasting, deal tracking.</li> <li>Driving activation: not just closing, but ensuring new business customers are fully set up, onboarded, and are using Monzo for their banking needs.</li> <li>Collaborating internally: work closely with marketing, product, risk and customer operations to ensure a smooth journey for customers.</li> <li>Delivering outstanding service at every touchpoint: via phone, video, email or digital channels.</li> <li>Achieving sales targets: conversion, activations, revenue, engagement and other growth metrics as set by the commercial leadership.</li> <li>Feeding insights back: capture and share customer feedback — customer pain points, required features, suggestions for product improvements.</li> <li>Adapting & iterate: Things will change rapidly and often - you’ll need to be comfortable with ambiguity and change and help support what comes next.</li> </ul> <p><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if you...</strong></p> <ul> <li>Have experience in Small Business sales, ideally selling business solutions or financial services; knowing how to engage business customers and understand their mindset, needs and pain points.</li> <li>Have a proven track record of meeting (or exceeding) sales quotas / targets in a performance-driven environment.</li> <li>Are an expert at managing a full sales cycle: from prospecting to activation, including structured and rigorous outreach and follow-ups and cross-team coordination.</li> <li>Have high emotional intelligence and are able to quickly connect and build a relationship with customers of diverse backgrounds and levels of knowledge.</li> <li>Are a strategic communicator,  excellent at building trust and helping customers discover value - you’re consultative, you listen, you ask insightful questions.</li> <li>Are adaptable and resilient, you embrace change and have a strong winning mindset to see challenges as opportunities to learn and grow.</li> <li>Can communicate clearly: written, verbal, via video; you simplify complex topics for customers.</li> <li>Are coachable and comfortable seeking constructive criticism to empower continuous learning and improvement</li> <li>Are comfortable working in a fast-moving, high change environment. You thrive when things aren’t fully defined yet.</li> <li>Can demonstrate high levels of personal organisation: tracking your pipeline, managing your time, prioritising your leads and follow-up tasks.</li> <li>Have integrity and strong consumer duty awareness: regulatory compliance, knowing your customer, reducing risk, safeguarding data and ensuring we put consumer duty first are foundational to this role and our culture.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Bonus / Nice-to-haves:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Prior experience in a regulated environment (banking)</li> <li>Experience with Salesforce</li> <li>Familiarity with SMBs in specific verticals (e.g. food & drink, professional services, construction)</li> </ul> <p><strong>🙌 What’s in it for you</strong></p> <p>💰 £67,000 Total OTE (base salary + commission)</p> <p>📍 4 days a week in our London office but with occasional flexibility to work remotely (in the UK)</p> <p>⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team. </p> <p>📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.</p> <p>🏡 We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given Macbooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup. </p> <p>➕ Plus lots more! <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">Read our full list of benefits</a>.</p> <p><strong>🌈 The application journey has the following key steps</strong></p> <ul> <li>Phone call with recruiter (30 mins)</li> <li>Sales experience video interview with Sales Lead (45 mins)</li> <li>In-person assessment: Practical task assessment + Team and Culture fit interview (90 mins)</li> </ul> <p>This process should take around 4-6 weeks - your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible! </p> <p>We have some guidelines on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to ace an application and interview at Monzo 🤖 <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/the-ultimate-guide-on-using-ai-to-ace-an-interview-at-monzo">You can read them here.</a></p> <p>#LI-NZ1</p><div class="content-conclusion"><hr> <p><strong>Equal opportunities for everyone</strong></p> <p>Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo.
